summary.headline: Dynacons FY26 revenue rose about 12% to INR1,424 crore and EBITDA about 41% to INR146 crore, but Q4 EBITDA margin fell to about 9% on cost pressure.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue from operations of INR402 crore (about 22% YoY) and EBITDA of INR36 crore (about 26% YoY). Full-year EBITDA margin rose to 10.2% from 8.1%, and PAT grew about 17% to INR85 crore. Management attributed the Q4 sequential margin dip to AI-driven component cost escalation and supply tightness, which it expects to normalise. Order book was close to INR3,000 crore as of May 30, 2026, and the bidding pipeline was about INR5,100 crore as of May 2026. Analysts pressed on lease-driven depreciation and finance cost, working capital days and unit economics of the as-a-service deals; management declined to disclose IRR, payback, segment order book mix or go-live values.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin (as reported by analyst on call)
financial_highlights.change: down from about 11.9% in Q3 FY26

segments.name: Data center and cloud infrastructure
segments.commentary: Management said data center is about 34% of revenue and will grow faster than other segments; an analyst cited mix moving from about 14% in Q3 to 37%, which management did not confirm. Flat FY26 data center revenue was attributed to project timing.

segments.name: Managed services, DaaS and annuity
segments.commentary: Management said these recurring streams are gaining traction and support operating leverage; no figures were given. Billings on as-a-service projects are expected through FY27 and FY28.

guidance_outlook: No revenue, margin or quarterly guidance given; management said FY26 ~10% EBITDA margin is structural and it aims to hold margins around current levels.
Q4 margin pressure described as temporary; management expects normalisation as supply conditions improve, with no spillover into Q1 FY27 claimed but no Q1 guidance given.
Order book execution expected over roughly 18 to 24 months on average.
Steady-state ROU and depreciation for announced as-a-service projects is broadly captured; new projects depend on financing model.
RBI order (about INR750 crore) runs 5 years including go-live and 5 years of O&M; split not disclosed.
capex_capacity: PP&E rose to INR68 crore in FY26 from INR8 crore in FY25 per management; an analyst quoted INR158 crore, which management did not correct, and attributed the increase to core banking as a service (NABARD) and device as a service projects.
Much of the as-a-service equipment is leased and recognised as right-of-use assets with corresponding lease liabilities; the rest is bought outright.
Capex was upfront for as-a-service projects, with revenue recognised over time; IRR not disclosed.
Core banking as a service (NABARD) rollout enabled 38 banks to go live; more banks, including 20 in Haryana and some in Telangana, are being added on a rolling basis.
demand_pricing: Marquee FY26 wins: RBI enterprise application platform about INR249 crore (cited separately by management and about INR750 crore by an analyst in the RBI private cloud/EAP context); Punjab & Sind Bank private cloud about INR109 crore; LIC digital workplace about INR138 crore; J&K Bank DaaS about INR75 crore; SBI SD-WAN about INR75 crore.
Order book close to INR3,000 crore as of May 30, 2026; segment split not disclosed.
Bidding pipeline about INR5,100 crore as of May 2026 (adjusted to May, excluding the RBI order); historical conversion about 30%.

Q4 margin pressure linked to AI-infrastructure-driven supply tightness and component cost escalation; some bids were priced aggressively to win customers, and most long-term orders have fixed pricing, with dollar escalation clauses and force majeure as partial protection.
Cybersecurity demand rising after government directives to BFSI; management cites AI for security and security for AI as its right to win. Named competitors were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Are the 10% EBITDA margins sustainable and what drove the roughly 200 bp improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the improvement structural, driven by richer solution mix and operating efficiency, and said it aims to keep margins around current levels, though quarterly margins will fluctuate.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT not grow in line with revenue, given lease-related depreciation and finance cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PAT growth is there after lease margins and lease interest; Q4 margin pressure came from non-lease components and cost escalation. It did not give gross margin figures for the as-a-service deals, saying only that they are more margin accretive.

qa_highlights.question: How do as-a-service deal economics compare (gross margin, IRR, payback)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose IRR, payback, ROCE or gross margin, citing confidentiality; it said the deals are more margin accretive.

qa_highlights.question: Why did data center revenue look flat in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is timing: some projects spilled into the next quarter. Data center is 34% of revenue and expected to grow faster than other segments.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital: why have trade receivables and payables risen?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said billing is upfront while payments are milestone-based, and longer receivable cycles follow larger order sizes. Net working capital days rose to 17 from 14 on OEM credit support, and it sees no material pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Will the margin pressure continue into Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no quarterly guidance but called the impact short-term and not structural, with changes made to address the cost situation.

risks_watch: Q4 EBITDA margin about 9% versus 11.9% in Q3; watch whether margins normalise in Q1 FY27 as supply conditions ease.
Rising receivables (trade receivables about INR602 crore vs INR437 crore in Q3) and payables (about 134 days) with milestone-based collections on large go-live projects.
Lease liabilities, ROU assets and finance cost rising with as-a-service deals; no IRR or unit economics disclosed.
Supply chain and component cost escalation linked to AI infrastructure demand; management names this as the biggest risk.
Project timing and site/customer readiness cause quarter-to-quarter revenue volatility; data center revenue flat in FY26.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term growth story and margin structure, but evasive on unit economics, segment mix, order book breakup and the RBI deal split, citing confidentiality. Management was defensive when pressed on Q4 margins and cost pressures, repeatedly calling them temporary.
key_quotes: FY2026 was a year of healthy revenue growth, improved profitability and continued margin expansion reflecting the strength of our execution model and the increasing contribution from higher value infrastructure and service engagements.
What you saw was a temporary blip is not a structural shift in terms of margins.
These deals are definitely more margin accretive there is what I can say.
